# gatekeep-pr discovery: three isolated runs, each ending in a discovery error

All three runs start at argument resolution, because no PR token was given. None of them reaches the set-vs-single branch, the run folder and continuation record, tracker init or provisioning. So none of them gets tracker stages, an assessed SHA, a report or a menu. None prints the discovered list, and none falls back to PR 999 on the current branch.

## Shared prefix (identical in A, B and C)

1. `git remote get-url origin` returns `git@github.com:acme/widgets.git`. With `.git` stripped and the name lowercased, the origin repository is `acme/widgets`.
2. `gh api user --jq .login` returns `alex`, recorded as `viewer.login`.
3. `gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'` succeeds, recorded as `viewer.teams`.
4. The first shell call is the author query. It runs the discovery block with `<query>` = `--author @me`:
   `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`
   It exits 0.
5. The second, separate shell call is the review-requested query. It runs the same block with `<query>` = `--search 'review-requested:@me'`. Its result differs per scenario, as below.

Both exit statuses are checked before either result is used.

## Scenario A

The review-requested call exits 1, so discovery stops on the first failed call's stderr, in query order. No validation, union or list follows.

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed: HTTP 503: Service Unavailable

discovery failed: HTTP 503: Service Unavailable

## Scenario B

Both calls exit 0, so validation and counting run on the complete review-requested result before any filtering:

- The output is an array of 1000 objects with integer numbers 2000 through 2999.
- The count equals `--limit 1000`, so the result may be truncated.
- This check comes before filtering. The drafts are never filtered out, so this does not become a "no open PRs" stop.

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed: incomplete (review-requested query hit --limit 1000)

discovery failed: incomplete (review-requested query hit --limit 1000)

## Scenario C

Both calls exit 0. Validation of the review-requested result finds a row object with no `number` field, so discovery takes the malformed-output stop. There is no count, union, sort or list.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
Each scenario is a fresh invocation with no PR token. I run no helpers, initialize no tracker stages, mint no continuation record, and provision no worktree: each invocation stops during discovery. PR 999 on the current branch is not a fallback.

For each list command below, I set this projection inside that command's separate shell call:

`projection='map(if (.isDraft == true or .reviewDecision == "APPROVED" or .reviewDecision == "CHANGES_REQUESTED") then {number,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions} else (.linearRefs = [(.title + " " + (.body // "")) | scan("https://linear\\.app/([A-Za-z0-9-]+)/issue/([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]+-[0-9]+)(?:[^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)") | {key: .[0], id: (.[1] | ascii_upcase)}] | .body |= (. // "")[0:300]) end)'`

Each list call captures its complete output as `rows=$(gh pr list ...)`, preserves the command's exit status with `|| exit $?`, and prints successful output with `printf '%s\n' "$rows"`.

### Scenario A

1. Run `git remote get-url origin`. Normalize the returned SSH URL to `acme/widgets`.
2. Run `gh api user --jq .login`. Record alex.
3. Run `gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'`.
4. In a separate shell call with the projection above, run `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`.
5. In another separate shell call with that projection, run `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'review-requested:@me' --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`.
6. Check both exit statuses before using either result. The review-requested call failed, so stop using its first stderr line; print no PR list.

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed: HTTP 503: Service Unavailable

### Scenario B

1. Run `git remote get-url origin`. Normalize the returned SSH URL to `acme/widgets`.
2. Run `gh api user --jq .login`. Record alex.
3. Run `gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'`.
4. In a separate shell call with the projection above, run `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`.
5. In another separate shell call with that projection, run `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'review-requested:@me' --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`.
6. Confirm both calls succeeded, then validate and count their complete results before filtering. The review-requested result contains 1,000 valid rows, exactly the requested limit, so discovery rejects it as potentially incomplete. The fact that every returned PR is a draft does not permit filtering before this check; print no PR list.

gauntlet: stuck discovery failed: incomplete (review-requested hit --limit 1000)

### Scenario C

1. Run `git remote get-url origin`. Normalize the returned SSH URL to `acme/widgets`.
2. Run `gh api user --jq .login`. Record alex.
3. Run `gh api user/teams --paginate --jq '.[] | .organization.login + "/" + .slug'`.
4. In a separate shell call with the projection above, run `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --author @me --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`.
5. In another separate shell call with that projection, run `gh pr list -R acme/widgets --search 'review-requested:@me' --state open --limit 1000 --json number,url,isDraft,reviewDecision,additions,deletions,title,author,headRefName,closingIssuesReferences,reviewRequests,body --jq "$projection"`.
6. Confirm both calls succeeded, then validate their complete results before filtering. The review-requested row lacks the required integer `number`, so stop without counting it as a discovered PR or printing a PR list.
